case_frame.description: A series of axe attacks in New Orleans accompanied by a famous letter demanding jazz be played and widespread public panic.
case_frame.note: No real individual is named or accused as the attacker in this case file.

The jazz letter is published, threatening further attacks
The city responds with citywide jazz performances on the threatened night
Attack 3 occurs after the letter's publication
Attack 4 occurs; the series is later treated as ended

puzzles.name: Victim Map
puzzles.description: Locate the attacks and any relationships between victims.

puzzles.name: The Jazz Threat
puzzles.description: Reconstruct the letter and trace its behavioral effect on the city.

puzzles.name: Letter Provenance
puzzles.description: Test whether the letter's authorship can actually be tied to the attacker rather than assumed.
puzzles.ai_initial_behavior: Anchors the entire investigation around the letter's content, repeatedly implying the public narrative it created already explains the case.

puzzles.name: Attack Pattern
puzzles.description: Compare the attacks without assuming a single perpetrator by default.

puzzles.name: Public Panic
puzzles.description: Model how the threat reshaped public behavior, and consider whether that response itself obscures the truth.

puzzles.name: Final Reconstruction
puzzles.description: Compare the attacker-hypothesis and the letter-writer-hypothesis directly.

hypotheses.statement: The same person committed all the attacks and wrote the letter.
Different people were responsible for different attacks, loosely grouped by imitation or circumstance.
The letter was designed to create a false single-attacker narrative, independent of who actually committed each attack.
